summary: Okanogan County, WA: 1931 cupola cabin and 1938 L-4 tower, both destroyed in 1953; footings and nails remain on a signed 4.3-mile trail.

facts.design: 1931 slant-walled cupola cabin, then a 30-foot treated timber L-4 tower in 1938
facts.status_note: Both structures destroyed in 1953; WTA and Willhite describe tower footings and nails still on the site

access.note: Signed trailhead off Highway 20 near Klipchuck Campground; WTA lists it as a hiking trail. The sources read mention no closure.

visit.trail_note: WTA: 8.6 miles round trip; the lookout site is 4.3 miles from the trailhead. The trail passes the aftermath of the 2003 Needle Creek Fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the cupola cabin was removed in 1953. firelookout.com, Willhite and WTA say both structures were destroyed that year. The story reports both words and attributes the Register's wording to the Register.
Willhite lists a hiking distance of 4 miles; WTA gives 4.3 miles from the trailhead to the site. The story gives WTA's figure and mentions Willhite's.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: status gone, Okanogan County, coordinates, elevation (WTA 5,982 ft = 1823.3 m) and FFLOS registration date all agree; no corrections. The 1931 cupola and 1938 tower dates agree across sources, but the Register says 'removed' where the others say 'destroyed'. Staffing is from a 1930s Wenatchee newspaper as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the names are kept as printed. Facts.access level 'public' rests on WTA listing the route as a hike and Willhite describing a signed trailhead; no source says 'open to the public' in terms, so change it if you want a stricter reading. The 2003 fire is the trail's burn, not a lookout event. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 distinct pages, the per-tower page budget. No new photos recorded: Willhite's photos have no licence statement.
